about: Built by tools/build_chateau.py. The grounds come from OpenStreetMap; floors 1 and 2 are traced from the Historic American Buildings Survey’s measured drawings of 1970 (HABS RI-313), turned so north is up, with room names from the HABS description. The restroom’s place comes from HABS (the Preservation Society doesn’t say where it is); the Chinese Moon Gate is approximate. Floors 3, 4 and the basement are not on the tour.
source: OpenStreetMap (grounds), Historic American Buildings Survey RI-313 (plans and room descriptions of floors 1 and 2), the Preservation Society of Newport County’s accessibility page (visitor facilities)
units: grounds: metres x 2.4, north up; house: pixels of the HABS sheets x 0.6, turned north up

rooms.name: Porte-cochère on the north side: the front door, 9 steps up to the main floor
Vestibule: the outer double doors “disappear” into the wall panels; eight low marble steps up to the hall

Great Hall (the “tapestry hall”) and grand stair: three storeys high under a coloured-glass skylight, with Eastlake oak woodwork, bronze figures on the newel posts and a painted Tree of Life climbing the stair
rooms.label: Great Hall

rooms.label: Green Parlor

rooms.name: Library: carved walnut by Luigi Frullini (dated 1873), with “Colombo” and “Amerigo” on the pilasters; one bookcase swings open into the Billiard Room
